causeEvidence: The old development diagnostic kept every historical TextureSource in a strong Set.
Installed Pixi8.14.0 TextureSource.destroy nulls resource, but source.options.resource still references the original image. A retained diagnostic source can therefore retain its decoded bitmap.

Production-mode controlled Chrome page: strong-observer scenario reached426MB tab memory; after clearing only diagnostic references and requesting GC the observed tab value later reached211MB; weak-observer scenario showed220MB after the same12 switches. These are sampled contextual readings, not a benchmark or a device-memory guarantee.
change: Assets-loaded ImageBitmap ownership is registered once per shared TextureSource using a WeakSet.
At source destruction the decoded bitmap is explicitly closed. Atlas-view destruction, pause and GPU unload do not close a still-live shared bitmap.
All four render image load paths register ownership, including image-success/metadata-failure atlas cleanup. Fallback images and environments without ImageBitmap retain previous behavior.
The diagnostic observer now defaults to WeakRef; strong mode remains as a retained-object stress control.
